targets.text: the strategist changes configuration, not minds: typed, gated, tested and revertible prompt/example/verification changes replace advisory directives; the worker is unaware of the strategist; senses relays the world to the embodiment and the inner state to the world; no default changes until the config-change arm is measured against the advisory arm and the ungoverned control

the shipped rig stays untouched until a pre-registered verdict supports promotion: the redesigned tier ships opt-in and off, an INCONCLUSIVE result leaves the rig as-is, and this time the rule is held by a real governance guard (test_governance.py currently has none for the strategist)

the strategist's output unit becomes a typed configuration change - prompt change, code-example change, verification-rule change - each type with its own schema, its own gate and its own test, per issue #75; the 'gated and tested' clause carries the entire safety story because configuration authority is strictly stronger than directive authority
a change type without its own schema, its own gate and its own test does not ship - 'gated and tested' is verifiable per type, not a slogan on the tier

`loop.py` stays zero-diff and the unarmed path stays byte-identical to `run()`: the README pins this three ways (signature refuses an invented keyword, host objects forwarded by identity, AST walk of the actor's transitive import closure shows no scope module reachable) and it was confirmed live with all-zero counters - the redesign must preserve all three pins

provable, not asserted: the existing suite plus the AST import-closure test stay green unmodified, and an unarmed governor still forwards the host's objects by identity - the same three pins that hold today hold after the redesign

the senses half of #75 (relays the world to the embodiment and the inner state to the world) is colleague's surface, not embodiment's: README's scope note says 'embodiment frames cortex, not senses' with the split recorded on colleague#352 - any senses-half work is a proposal filed on colleague, never pushed
no change of this frame touches colleague: every senses-half change lands either in embodiment's host-owned surfaces or as a filed colleague issue - checkable in the delivery record

ratchet prevention is a first-class requirement with its own pre-registered measurement condition: advice evaporates, configuration accumulates - successive changes each passing their gate can compound badly, and the failure already appeared in miniature in the advisory design when a one-off task instruction became a durable persisted constraint (live session §4.2, #66)

compounding is detectable, not assumed away: successive gate-passing changes are re-evaluated against a fixed baseline so drift each individual gate misses still shows, and reverting to baseline is always possible

every applied configuration change is revertible and its effect observable under C3: a subtly worse prompt is the most silent degradation available, so apply/rollback are recorded transitions and detection of degraded behaviour is part of the design, not an operator hope
no configuration change degrades silently: every apply and revert is a recorded transition, and the host can observe that behaviour changed because configuration changed (C3)

value is measured before any default changes: a ScopeBench re-run with a config-change arm against the advisory arm against the ungoverned control, same seven-condition verdict rule plus a new ratchet condition and a new absent-cell reason; fixing #58 (`SCOPE_AUTHORITY` never states the scope_id-must-be-new rule) is a precondition for the advisory arm to be a fair comparator - 47 of 93 proposals refused as duplicates voided 32 of 36 cells of the layer control last time

the verdict rule is committed before any dial and one ABSENT condition forces INCONCLUSIVE, which leaves the shipped rig untouched - the same rule that kept the muse and the advisory strategist out of the reference rig

the redesigned tier ships opt-in and off under a real governance guard this time: today the strategist appears nowhere in `tests/test_governance.py` (0 occurrences; the guards are muse-surface, worker-promotion, drones-opt-in) - CLAUDE.md's claim that the file enforces the strategist rule is drift; the actual enforcement is structural (`ScopeGovernor.armed` + AST zero-import tests) - the muse/drone guard templates (promotion flag + cited verdict, or env opt-in + AST single-bypass, each with a test-of-the-test) are the pattern to copy
the guard can go red (a TestTheseGuardsCanFail case proves it) and CLAUDE.md's drifted claim that test_governance.py already enforces the strategist rule is corrected in the same change

the gate policy is empirically derived per change type during development and benchmarking, with a three-way verdict fixed before any dial: a change type that works well is allowed without gating; one that breaks easily gets a protection designed and gated; one too easy to break or degrade is shut off for now - the verdict is a measured outcome per type, not a fixed upfront policy

the three-way verdict rule (allow ungated / gate / shut off) is committed per change type BEFORE any dial, and every change type's verdict is recorded beside the measurement that produced it - a verdict rule written after seeing results is not a gate
the strategist's configuration surface is: the worker's tools, prompts, knowledge, and permissions (what it is allowed to do); and the senses seat's prompts, permissions, and basic knowledge

every configuration change routes through host-owned configuration surfaces - the host's injected ToolExecutor and approval policy are never bypassed, and a change unit with an unknown shape is refused whole and recorded, never partially applied
the ScopeBench comparison runs before any lane decision: the advisory lane survives as the comparator arm until the config-change arm is measured against it and the ungoverned control

the advisory lane stays importable and dialable until the comparison lands; #58's SCOPE_AUTHORITY gap is fixed before the advisory arm runs so it is a fair comparator; and the pre-registration names the senses checkpoint delta (coolthor NVFP4A16 -> unsloth QAT w4a16) as a rig confound

the after-state is an assistant or companion you can and want to work with - a diverse mind entity: multiple model families cooperating as one teammate, validated by overall live-testing and not only by bench conditions

companion-grade is judged in live testing against a matched ungoverned control (the session-1 protocol, now #73), not only on bench episodes - and the wording stays C2-honest: diverse minds are an architectural fact shown in traces, one teammate is what the operator addresses

the strategist improves the rig by changing configuration in the background - the worker and senses seats simply operate under better tools, prompts, knowledge and permissions - and what the operator experiences is an assistant or companion they can and want to work with: a diverse mind entity

the after-state is demonstrated end-to-end on a non-colleague host (issue #2's definition-of-done rule) and judged in live session 2 against a matched ungoverned control, not asserted from bench cells alone

hosts that embed embodiment (colleague, the reachy family, greenhouse-style example apps) plus this repo's own example hosts and ScopeBench harnesses; the operator arms the strategist explicitly, and end operators keep experiencing one coherent teammate
a host can wire the tier from documented seams alone - the #62/#58-class traps either ship fixed or are documented at the seam, so a correct-looking wiring cannot silently produce an incapable tier

the advisory design puts a persuasion problem in the loop and the only matched control measured it buying nothing: 189.6 s and 3663 strategist tokens for zero applied directives and a materially identical answer, with 69.5% of session tokens buying restatement or nothing - configuration change replaces advice that can be ignored with inputs that are actually different
the motivating numbers stay cited as what they are - n=1 on one rig with one model pair, a report not a measurement - and are never inflated into 'proven worthless' any more than 'proven valuable'

the config-change arm separates from both the advisory arm and the ungoverned control under a pre-registered verdict rule that includes a ratchet condition - and in live testing the governed rig produces a measurably better session than the matched ungoverned control, instead of session 1's materially-identical-at-higher-cost result

separation means the pre-registered margins under the committed verdict rule; a tie or an ABSENT cell reads INCONCLUSIVE and ships nothing - the same rule that kept the muse and the advisory strategist out of the rig

promoting the worker to the acting seat crosses the shipped worker-promotion gate: tests/test_governance.py's TestWorkerRolePromotionGate blocks a worker row in the CLAUDE.md/README rig tables while _WORKER_ROLE_HAS_SUPPORTING_VERDICT is False, and no committed verdict supports acting-seat promotion today (the worker measurements on record are throughput/overhead/seam, and ScopeBench's worker-dependent cells fell below the protocol floor) - promotion happens through the gate with a cited measured verdict, never by editing the gate away

the flag flips only in the same change that cites a docs/live-test-results/ verdict actually supporting the worker as acting loop; the t24 truncation lesson transfers to whichever seat acts (the worker's finish_reason is equally absent, #37)

the worker may write the senses seat's knowledge - a designated, schema-distinct block of what composes senses' context (arguably part of the prompt, deliberately designated as its own surface) - but never senses' prompts; prompt authority over senses belongs to the strategist alone

the designation is structural, not conventional: the knowledge block is a schema-distinct surface the worker writes through a defined seam, senses' prompt text is unreachable from any worker-writable surface, and a worker-originated write to a prompt-shaped target is a refused shape, recorded

the worker-to-senses knowledge channel is attributed, because it is a path from the acting tier to the operator's ear: every knowledge-block entry carries origin attribution as a required field, and senses' framing states that knowledge entries are attributed claims - the #63 record shows senses relays what it is given and defers under pressure, so an unattributed channel would let a compromised or fabricating acting tier put words in the interaction tier's mouth anonymously (the config-design analogue of the t6/#55 surrender direction)

a knowledge entry with no origin attribution is a refused shape, recorded; a fabricated or injected entry is traceable to its writer in the ledger; and the senses grounding clause covers the knowledge block explicitly (knowledge is attributed claims, not the seat's own perception)

the config-change ledger schema is versioned and fail-closed against advisory-era persisted state: a host whose ScopePersistence payload holds an advisory directive chain gets a recorded refusal or ignore with a version hint - never a silent reinterpretation of old state under new semantics, never a crash into the host's main path
a config-design host pointed at an advisory-era state file degrades visibly (one recorded degradation, actor continues unconfigured) - exercised by test with a real advisory-era payload fixture

an operator-visible introspection surface reports each seat's current effective configuration with provenance - which change produced it, when, under which gate verdict - derived from the applied-change ledger (one source of truth, no parallel bookkeeping), so any operator-visible utterance can be traced to the configuration active when it was produced; this is the running-system capability introspection issue #75 itself names as missing, and it is also what makes a revert honest: revert restores configuration, not the world, and the record shows which config each past utterance rode
the introspection output is derived from the applied-change ledger and nothing else; a config state the ledger cannot explain is itself a recorded degradation (C3)

config changes apply through propose -> verify -> apply: a change (prompt changes are the named instance) is first a proposal; a test suite verifies it against the affected seat; it applies only when that seat is available for testing, not in a run, and the suite passed - so the session continues mid-drive while no seat ever has its configuration changed under it mid-run

a seat that is mid-run never observes a config change: apply is atomic between runs for that seat, making the advisory design's constant-sha mechanism check per-seat (config constant within any single run, changes only between runs); a proposal whose suite fails is never applied and the failure is recorded, like a failed drone smoke

the knowledge block rides eidetic - no parallel memory system: worker writes and strategist maintenance land as eidetic records in a designated scope, senses reads via recall, and the strategist/cortex maintains the store over time (consolidation, supersession, ageing decisions) - eidetic owns memory mechanics, embodiment owns when entries are written, recalled and revisited in the lived sequence (issue #2's split, applied)

no second knowledge store drifts into existence: the knowledge block is eidetic records under a designated scope, c30's origin attribution rides eidetic's native provenance rather than a new invented field, and a knowledge write that bypasses eidetic is a refused shape

the result is published whichever way it comes back; a failed probe is a named trigger for /deviate on the three-tier decision, not a quiet retry

Copy docs/live-test-results/cortex-toolcall-probe.md's pattern, point it at the worker role via the lobes gateway, and script it (never inline one-liners). Derive every clock from max_tokens/rate per tests/rate_config.py - a clock sized against the wrong quantity becomes the measurement. Coordinate rig time with the operator before dialling.

acceptance_criteria: propose/verified/applied are distinct recorded states; apply is gated on seat-idle plus suite-pass

acceptance_criteria: reverting to baseline is always possible and exercised by test
successive gate-passing changes can be re-evaluated against the fixed baseline, so drift each individual gate misses is detectable

a config state the ledger cannot explain is itself a recorded degradation (C3)

acceptance_criteria: README and explain document the tier as opt-in and off, state the no-determinism wording (the change is deterministic, the effect is not) and the C2 'diverse mind entity' discipline, and document both known trap classes at the seam

tasks.instruction: Every number cited names its n and its rig. Negative and INCONCLUSIVE results are stated as such. Do not let 'deterministic' back into the wording: the change is deterministic, the effect is not.

risks.text: cross-type composition: two individually-gated changes composing into an effect no gate evaluated - the pre-registration must address it or declare it out of its scope explicitly
capability-id enumeration: no enumerable capability catalog seam exists in the loop contract; how ids are enumerated and kept stable across hosts and restarts must be resolved during schema design
worker acting feasibility: if the t1 probe fails, the acting-seat promotion and the three-tier decision c26 are invalidated - the named response is /deviate, never a quiet retry or model swap

rig contention: bench and live-session tasks dial the operator's rig (local cortex, proxied worker and senses) - scheduling is the operator's call, and the t24/finish_reason truncation trap applies to every dialled seat
